subject: Dependency stewardship & supply‑chain ownership — attestation deliverables
messages:
From: Anna Singh <anna.singh@cedarhealth.io>
To: jonas.weber@redwood.ai
Cc: 
Date: Wed, 20 Jan 2027 10:12:00 -0800
Subject: Request: runtime dependency ownership and supply-chain attestation

Jonas,

Thanks for taking this. CedarHealth is collecting a short attestation package ahead of procurement sign‑off. We need the following by EOD Jan 27 so our compliance team can complete the SIG/CAIQ review:

- A current subprocessor roster (CSV) with owner (team/person), purpose, data exposure (PHI/PII/none), residency (region/country), and whether tokenization/ephemeral keys are used.
- Answers to SIG/CAIQ controls related to key management, data residency, and vendor access (you can point us to an existing pack if you have one).
- Evidence: your latest SOC 2 Type II report, KMS architecture diagram showing ownership and residency, and any contractual flow (DPA/processor mapping) you can share.

Specific asks related to the inference runtime: please confirm who owns the KV cache provider, model registry persistence, and whether any third‑party binaries or hosted artifacts are pulled at runtime (and from where).

If you prefer a secure share, we can provide a presigned transfer. Otherwise, DocuSign/SharePoint links are fine. Our security lead (cc'd on follow‑ups) will attend a short alignment call if needed.

Appreciate a short plan and point of contact.

—Anna
Security & Procurement
CedarHealth

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Anna Singh <anna.singh@cedarhealth.io>
Cc: karthik.iyer@redwood.ai, grace.oconnor@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 20 Jan 2027 13:08:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: runtime dependency ownership and supply-chain attestation

Anna — thanks for the clear list.

Quick plan:
- Attached: preliminary subprocessor roster (redwood_prelim_subprocessor_roster_20270120.csv). This is exportable as a CSV and contains owner and residency columns; it's focused on runtime dependencies (KV cache, model store, artifact fetchers) and infra providers.
- We'll produce a SIG/CAIQ slice that maps to your asked controls and bundle the SOC 2 Type II report and KMS diagram by Jan 25. If we can get a hard deadline of Jan 27 for final sign‑off, that works for us.
- I'll schedule a 30‑minute sync on Jan 24 to walk through the KV cache and KMS residency controls — I'll invite our security engineer (Karthik) and product owner (Grace).

Attachments: redwood_prelim_subprocessor_roster_20270120.csv (preview attached)

If CedarHealth prefers an SFTP/presigned link for the full pack, let me know and we'll send one.

Best,
Jonas Weber
Security Liaison, Redwood Inference

From: Anna Singh <anna.singh@cedarhealth.io>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: karthik.iyer@redwood.ai, grace.oconnor@redwood.ai, security@cedarhealth.io
Date: Thu, 21 Jan 2027 09:34:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: runtime dependency ownership and supply-chain attestation

Thanks Jonas — roster looks like a good start. Confirmed: the Jan 24 sync at 10:00 AM PST works for us; our compliance lead (Marco Lee) will dial in.

A couple of clarifications for the pack:
- We need explicit statements on ephemeral key usage during inference (e.g., are model keys ephemeral per‑request? do you use ephemeral tokenization for input payloads?).
- For any third‑party artifact pulls, please include the origin (e.g., public PyPI, internal vendor bucket) and whether signatures/checksums are validated.

We'll accept links to DocuSign/S3 presigned URLs for the SOC2 and KMS diagram. If you must redact specific contractual clauses, please note which sections were redacted and why.

Anna

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Anna Singh <anna.singh@cedarhealth.io>
Cc: jonas.weber@redwood.ai, grace.oconnor@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 25 Jan 2027 16:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Deliverables: CedarHealth SIG/CAIQ slice, SOC2 and KMS artefacts

Anna,

Following up from the sync on Jan 24 — attached are the deliverables we agreed to:

- redwood_sig_responses_q1_2027.pdf — curated SIG/CAIQ responses relevant to your control set (controls highlighted and mapped to runtime dependencies).
- redwood_soc2_typeii_2026.pdf — our most recent SOC 2 Type II report (redacted at a clause level for contractual sensitivity).
- kms-residency-diagram.png — high‑level KMS ownership and residency diagram showing the key escrow flow and HSM boundaries.
- redwood_prelim_subprocessor_roster_20270120.csv — updated with explicit runtime owner (product/inference) and PHI exposure column.

Notes / short answers:
- Ephemeral keys: we use short‑lived KMS‑issued ephemeral keys for session encryption of in‑flight payloads; persistent model encryption keys are rotated quarterly and stored in customer‑isolated KMS projects for Dedicated/Private customers. (See diagram and SIG control mappings in the PDF.)
- Third‑party artifact pulls: runtime images fetch prebuilt artifacts from our internal artifact registry (signed) and, in limited cases, from vetted vendor buckets; all artifacts are checksum‑verified at pull time.

Links/proofs:
- Atlassian ticket for the pack: https://redwoodinference.atlassian.net/browse/SEC-1543
- HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/CH-2027-0451

If you'd like a notarized copy or to deliver via secure transfer, tell us which method CedarHealth prefers and we'll provide it.

Regards,
Karthik Iyer
Senior Security Engineer
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood_sig_responses_q1_2027.pdf, redwood_soc2_typeii_2026.pdf, kms-residency-diagram.png, redwood_prelim_subprocessor_roster_20270120.csv
